* * *
About Joel Lambert

Joel Lambert spent 10 years as a Navy SEAL, during which he also served as a lead instructor at BUD/S.

After earning his Trident, he served his country, often operating deep behind enemy lines on missions few people ever hear about. He and his fellow SEALs lost friends along the way, but many others came back safely because of the unique skills and knowledge they gathered over the years.

And many of these skills are not military skills as you might think. They are the skills of our great-grandparents, the forgotten skills that once made Americans strong and independent.

The problem is that nobody teaches them anymore. 

Until now.

No matter if you’re 15 or 90, a man or a woman, this book turns you into a person who preserves the old ways and adds more value to the world.

* * *
They Just Don't Make Books Like This Anymore:




The Lost Skills of Independence is a beautiful, old-fashioned, hardcover book, with old school illustrations, so you can easily understand the skill without having to read through pages after pages of empty words.

You don't have to read the entire book all at once; you can just learn one or two new things every day while enjoying your coffee or tea, and pick it up where you left off some other day. Or, put this book on your coffee table — it's an instant conversation starter!

It also makes a great gift, especially between parents and children. When you gift this, you're passing down the skills that make them independent and self-reliant. What better gift to give than this?

The Lost Skills of Independence is organized in a very practical way. Instead of a boring table of contents, 200 illustrated skill cards with their page number, so you can easily find the one you're looking for.

For each skill, you'll find step-by-step instructions and full-color illustrations that easily guide you along the way. You also get a complete list of ingredients, materials or tools so you know exactly what you need upfront, without wasting any time.

Built with a durable hardcover and thick, high-quality paper that won't tear easily or wear down, so you can use these skills for the rest of your life. And, because it's spiral-bound, it stays open while your hands are busy.

* * *
Here Are Some Of The Skills You Will Find Inside:
Self-Sufficient Home Projects

These ingenious, easy-to-make projects will help you collect and store water, keep food cool, cook and even get hot water without electricity, grow your household food supply, and protect your essential supplies. 

You’ll turn ordinary materials into useful tools that can help you care for your family during long-term blackouts, economic crises, supply shortages, and other unexpected disruptions.

Most importantly, these projects help you prepare to live in a world without electricity.

Here are some of the projects you will find in this chapter:     

* How to Make an Off-Grid Refrigerator That Works Without Electricity  – This is perfect for long-term blackouts, if you want to live more self-sufficiently, and of course if you’re just trying to cut down on your power bills.

* How to Make Water Out of Thin Air – So, even when taps run dry, you’ll produce your own drinking water. 

* How to Stockpile a Ton of Water for 365 Days – Learn how to harvest and safely store an emergency water supply for your household.

* How a Trash Can Could Save You from an EMP – When other people will have no electricity, no working phones or cars, no refrigeration, no running water, your life will not change one bit.

* How to Build a Backyard Root Cellar from a Plastic Barrel – This will keep your food and medicine from spoiling even when there’s no electricity.

* How to Set Up Invisible DIY Alarms Against Intruders  – So you’ll always know when an intruder trespasses on your property.

* How to Use Plastic Bottles to Heat Your Home – You will discover how you can heat your home with bottles you normally throw away. This DIY heater takes advantage of the greenhouse effect inside the bottles, trapping and amplifying warmth like a mini solar furnace.

Lost Kitchen Secrets

In this chapter, you’ll discover how to build 3 months, 6 months, a year or more of long-lasting food supplies for blackouts, shortages, and emergencies. 

Explore wartime survival foods, filling meals that helped our grandparents through the Great Depression, and ingenious canning methods and forgotten preservation techniques that can keep foods for years without electricity. 

Here’s a glimpse of the kitchen secrets waiting for you inside:

* How to Make Pemmican – This superfood lasts for decades without refrigeration. A single pound packs over 3,500 calories, and because it's got protein, fat, and vitamins, you could live entirely on it!

* How to Make the Amish Burger in a Jar – For long term preservation instead of purchasing expensive survival food that has no taste nor enough proteins.

* How to Make the “Forever Sausage” – This delicious food earned its name because it doesn't spoil. This is what kept German pioneers alive on the Oregon trail when food was scarce and game meat unreliable, and will do the same for you when supermarkets go empty.

* The Little-Known Mistake That Ruins Cast Iron – If you see this, then you need to read this page as you can easily fix it.

* How to Make Crispy Amish Bread in a Jar – It's soft inside, crispy outside... and it tastes just like it came out of the oven!

* Grandma’s Great Depression Foods We Will All Need Again Soon – If these meals sustained families through one of the toughest times in our history, be sure they can do the same for you when the time comes.

* How to Make Yeast for Long-Term Storage – So shortages won’t stop you from putting fresh, crispy bread on your table every day.

* The Tricks to Making Eggs Last over 10 Years without Refrigeration – We will not use salt, brine, isinglass or any preservative. Eggs are cheap, lightweight, nutritious and, if it weren’t for their lack of Vitamin C, a person could basically live only on them for years.

Fundamental Survival Skills

In this chapter, you’ll discover skills to turn the wild into your second home. You will soon discover how to find water, build shelter, make fire, and make food using everything you have around you. 

Whether a crisis sends you into the woods or you enjoy camping and exploring, this knowledge helps you meet your daily needs and live more independently in nature.

Take a look at some of the survival skills included:

* How to Make the Ghost Fire – This is going to help you stay warm without being seen, cook and boil water without smoke giving you away.

* How to Build a Hidden Survival Shelter in the Wild – This one is a low-profile shelter built for brutal cold and long stays especially when you don't want to be seen. If you go in the wild, camping, or if a crisis ever forces you to leave your home, take this book with you! It will give you everything you need to survive out there, just like our ancestors who picked a place in the wild and made it their home.

* How to Build a Native American Smokehouse – This preserves meat safely for months (even years!) during long-term power outages.

* How to Turn Saltwater into Drinking Water – You will also discover how to turn saltwater into drinking water, a lost survival skill that will give you basically an endless supply of fresh water no matter what happens around us.

* How to Make the Swedish Fire – That turns a single log into a stove that burns for almost a full day.

* How to Make Yourself Invisible – So you can stay out of sight and avoid unwanted attention during a crisis.

* How to Build a Stone Oven in the Wild – So you can cook warm, filling meals without gas or electricity whenever you need to.

Lost Healing Secrets

In this chapter, you’ll discover how to make natural remedies using common ingredients you may already have at home. You get powerful recipes for everyday aches, joint comfort, gut troubles, skin care, liver health, basically every part of your body. 

You will be able to recreate the home remedies our grandparents relied on, and save some of the money you would spend at a pharmacy.

Here are some of the remedies included in this chapter:

* Nature’s “Painkiller” Hiding in Your Backyard – This common backyard plant that has a white sap that looks like the one in the opium poppy. Its painkilling effects are milder, but the plant is perfectly legal to harvest and use.

* How to Make Grandma’s Defense Tonic – The only remedy you need in your house during the cold season.

* What Happens When You Pour Honey Over Garlic – Grandmothers relied on this lost recipe long before pharmacies became mainstream to get over colds and other common ailments.

* What Happens When You Smoke Mullein – Mullein is known as a "breathing herb," so you can use it to support comfortable breathing during harsh seasons.

* Parasites Lurking in Your Gut Hate THIS – Most people throw them away, not realizing they contain potent enzymes that help flush out these nasty intruders from the body.

* The Stop-Bleeding Powder – This is a forgotten battlefield remedy that was successfully used during the Civil War. All you need are two common ingredients you probably have in your backyard right now.

Independent Living Skills

The skills covered in this chapter will help you handle everyday problems. These will help you become more independent, protect your privacy, and turn your home into the safest place on earth for you and your family.

Here’s a preview of the ingenious things you will read about:

* How to Detect Hidden Mics or Cameras Inside Your House or Office – So you can protect your privacy without expensive surveillance equipment.

* How to Cool Your Home without Electricity – This one shows you a handful of clever old-world methods that can help pull hot air out, trap cool air in, and make your home far more livable when the grid fails or the heat becomes unbearable.

* How to Fix a Stuck Zipper – You can do this in under a minute, using ordinary items you already have at home like a pencil, soap, or a dab of lip balm.

* Stop Throwing Away Wood Ash! Do This Instead! – Some people know it's a good fertilizer, but did you know there's five other ingenious uses for wood ash that nobody told you about and you will find in the book!

* How to Hide from Thermal Vision – You never know when this might save your life!

Self-Sustaining Garden

These practical gardening skills will help you grow more food in less space, improve your soil, collect water for irrigation, and extend your growing season. 

Turn a backyard, patio, or overlooked corner into a productive source of fresh vegetables, fruit, and useful herbs. 

You’ll discover practical ways to cut grocery costs and rely more on what you grow yourself!

Here are a few of the gardening skills waiting for you inside:

* How to Build a Hidden Food-Growing Fence with Pallets – This way, your idle fence can grow 150 pounds of fresh, chemical-free and utterly delicious foods under your neighbor’s nose. If folks had a food-growing fence like this one, everyone would be healthier, more prepared and keep more money in their pocket.

* How to Grow Fruit Trees in a Tiny Space – On a porch, a sunny windowsill, or along a small garden edge. They’re easy to care for and start producing fruit much faster than full-sized trees!

* How to Make a Straw Bale Garden – Straw bale gardening is a great way to grow plants in a tiny space and to have a fully compostable garden and a cheap and easy-to-build raised bed alternative. This is easy on the back as you don’t have to bend over to take care of your plants!

* How to Grow Food in Thin Air – This ingenious skill helps you grow your own food even if you don’t have space for a garden.

Life-Saving Skills

These skills prepare you to recognize danger and respond when quick decisions matter. You will be able to identify your emergency priorities before you need them!

Here are some of the emergency skills covered:

* How to EMP-Proof Your Car – While other cars will be completely useless, you'll be able to get around like nothing happened. The secret is a simple tweak that shields your car from total shutdown.

* Off-the-Radar Military Loopholes that You Can Use during Lockdowns, Civil Unrest and Martial Law – These are the kind of secrets you find out from a Navy Seals who has operated behind enemy lines, that you can use to avoid detection, bypass checkpoints, outsmart digital tracking, and the behavior that instantly puts you on watch lists when authorities start watching everyone.

* How to Break Out of Zip Ties – You will be able to do this in under a minute, using ordinary items you already have at home like a pencil, soap, or a dab of lip balm.

* What to Do If You’re Trapped in a Car – It could be a burning car that you need to exit quickly, a sinking car or if someone keeps you inside a car trunk. Even though it's unlikely you'll ever end up in these situations, these skills just take one minute to learn and you'll have them for life!

* How to Safely Remove a Tick – If you've ever wondered why you simply can't pull it out, here's why. The tick inserts a chainsaw-like needle covered in sharp, backward-facing barbs that act like a harpoon. The harder you pull, the more it gets stuck into your flesh. So, when you pull the body, the head can rip off and stay locked inside, causing infection. Instead of increasing your odds of Lyme, use the skill inside this book!

Forbidden Psychology

These skills help you recognize manipulation, respond to disrespect, gather useful information, and avoid being made responsible for someone else’s mistakes. 

Understand the patterns behind difficult conversations so you can respond with more clarity and control.

Here’s a glimpse of the psychology skills inside:

* How to Recognize and Deal with a Narcissist – The biggest mistake I see people make when dealing with a narcissist is calling them out. Now I know that feels like the right thing to do because you want to expose them, make them see what they're doing, and prove, to them and maybe even yourself, that you're not crazy. But the second you confront them, you don’t actually win...you just trigger them. The only way to win with a narcissist is stop playing their game and do this...

* How to Extract Useful Information Through Casual Conversation – This is so effective, the CIA uses it!

* How to Transfer Blame without Being Detected (The Art of Scapegoating) – Don’t do this if you want to be a good person! 

In every crisis, one person always ends up carrying the weight for everyone else. Inside the book, you’ll uncover the 5 dark principles that decide who becomes the scapegoat. Use this to never become one!

* How to Kill Disrespect Instantly – To set boundaries without escalating the situation.
